SECTION: Methodology (Pages 23-26)

TOPICS: survey methodology, panel recruitment, data collection, weighting process, sampling errors, response rates, demographic benchmarks

TEXT_EVIDENCE:
- The American Trends Panel (ATP) was created by Pew Research Center in 2014 through three recruitment waves in 2014, 2015, and 2017, with a total of 19,718 adults invited and 9,942 agreeing to participate (Page 23)
- Data is from a panel wave conducted April 29 to May 5, 2020 (Page 23)
- 10,957 out of 13,459 sampled panelists responded, for an 81% response rate (Page 23)
- The cumulative response rate accounting for nonresponse and attrition is 4.5% (Page 23)
- The margin of sampling error for the full sample is plus or minus 1.4 percentage points (Page 23)
- The study used a stratified random sample based on age, race, ethnicity, education, and other variables (Page 23)
- In August 2018, the ATP switched from telephone to address-based recruitment using the U.S. Postal Service's Delivery Sequence File (Page 24)
- Invitations were sent to a random, address-based sample (ABS) of households selected from the U.S. Postal Service's Delivery Sequence File (Page 24)
- A total of 9,396 were invited to join the panel in 2018, and 8,778 agreed and completed an initial profile survey (Page 24)
- The same procedure was carried out on August 19, 2019, with 5,900 invited and 4,720 agreeing to join (Page 24)
- Of the 23,440 individuals who have ever joined the ATP, 15,427 remained active panelists (Page 24)
- The U.S. Postal Service's Delivery Sequence File has been estimated to cover as much as 98% of the population (Page 24)
- The American Trends Panel never uses breakout routers or chains that direct respondents to additional surveys (Page 24)
- The ATP data was weighted using a multistep process starting with a base weight incorporating respondents' original selection probability (Page 25)
- The next step uses an iterative technique to align the sample to population benchmarks listed in the table (Page 25)
- Sampling errors and tests of statistical significance account for the effect of weighting (Page 25)
- Interviews are conducted in both English and Spanish (Page 25)
- Question wording and practical difficulties can introduce error or bias into opinion poll findings (Page 25)
- The table shows unweighted sample sizes and sampling errors at the 95% confidence level (Page 26)
- Total sample size is 10,957 with a margin of error of 1.4 percentage points (Page 26)
- The Rep/Lean Rep group has an unweighted sample size of 4,437, a weighted percentage of 44%, and a margin of error of 2.1 percentage points (Page 26)
- The Dem/Lean Dem group has an unweighted sample size of 6,182, a weighted percentage of 52%, and a margin of error of 2.0 percentage points (Page 26)
- Sample sizes and errors for other subgroups are available upon request (Page 26)
